title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 1 diabetes and peripheral neuropathy.

HPI
The patient is a long-term patient presenting for a routine follow-up of type 1 diabetes mellitus. They report stable management of blood glucose levels using a subcutaneous insulin regimen. The patient also reports persistent sensations of tingling and numbness in the lower extremities associated with polyneuropathy. The patient notes that these symptoms have been stable over the last three months.

Medication List
- Insulin (long-term use)

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical exam reveals diminished sensation to light touch in the bilateral feet. Reflexes are diminished at the ankles. No acute distress noted.

Assessment
1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus: Managed with insulin.
2. Polyneuropathy: The patient presents with symptoms of polyneuropathy. It is noted that this condition is unrelated to diabetes.

Plan
1. Continue current insulin regimen as prescribed.
2. Monitor for any changes in sensory symptoms related to the peripheral neuropathy.
3. Follow up in the clinic in three months for continued management.
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code each separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).
Do not assign Z79.4 for type 1 diabetes; insulin use is inherent.

distractors.why: Provider documentation of no link overrides the presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
Z79.4 is not assigned for type 1 diabetes.
